architecture.src/llm/base.py: provider-independent interface: Message, GenerationSettings, LLMResponse (final answer only), LLMError (provider-neutral kinds), LLMClient (retries with exponential backoff for retryable kinds, attempt counting, latency)
architecture.src/llm/groq_client.py: Groq provider via the official SDK; SDK retries disabled (max_retries=0); include_reasoning=False; Groq exceptions mapped to LLMError without provider message text; supported models openai/gpt-oss-20b and openai/gpt-oss-120b
architecture.src/llm/config.py: configuration from the process environment, then the Git-ignored .env (read without changing os.environ); key excluded from repr and records
architecture.src/llm/__init__.py: create_client(config) factory; application code never imports a provider SDK
architecture.src/evidence.py: read-only wrapper over the frozen Stage 6 retrieval (main and fallback configurations); returns top 5 with original chunk text, source, page, heading and ranking information
architecture.src/context.py: context builder (number, source, page, heading when present, original chunk text; scores and ranks not shown) and the S7-0 baseline grounded prompt (PROMPT_VERSION s7-0-baseline-v1, not optimised)
architecture.src/answer.py: answer_question(): question -> Stage 6 retrieval -> context -> LLM interface -> final answer, with the evidence returned alongside

eligibility.arm1: not eligible (hallucinations, groundedness, correctness, pairwise W-L -3)

results.selected_prompt: arm0 (s7-0-baseline-v1) retained: neither experimental arm qualified
results.instability: not flagged under the frozen thresholds (replicate |W-L| = 2 < 3; 1 question (N1) differs in correctness/hallucination < 3)
results.oos_S7_1B: all three arms 5/5 pass; 0 abstention failures; 0 serious failures
results.conclusiveness: treat_as_conclusive true under the frozen rules
results.observation: The Arm 0 replicate (identical prompt) showed the same groundedness total (27) and hallucination count (1) as Arms 1 and 2, so the experimental arms' failures on those two gates are of the same size as Arm 0's own run-to-run variation. Under the frozen thresholds the run is not flagged as unstable, and the frozen selection rule retains Arm 0. The result means neither experimental prompt demonstrated an improvement; it does not show Arm 0 is better than them.
results.wording: Arm 0 was retained under the predefined S7-1 criteria on a 15-question development subset; this is not proof and no held-out claim is made.

decision.statement: Neither Arm 1 nor Arm 2 satisfied the predefined replacement criteria. Arm 0 is not claimed to be proven intrinsically superior: the Arm 0 replicate demonstrated generation variability in groundedness and hallucination outcomes.
conclusions: Arm 1: pairwise wins-minus-losses = -3 and failed the replacement gates.
Arm 2: pairwise wins-minus-losses = -1 and failed the replacement gates.
Arm 0 replicate did not trigger the predefined instability threshold, but showed meaningful generation noise.
All 15 OOS evaluations appropriately abstained with zero invented MSU-specific information and zero general-knowledge answers.
S7-1 is development evidence only and makes no held-out performance claim.
limitations: Ceiling effect: 59/60 correctness and 60/60 completeness grades were 2; the decision rested on a few groundedness points and pairwise judgements.
Single sample per arm; the identical-prompt replicate differed from Arm 0 by as much as the experimental arms did on groundedness and hallucinations.
15-question development subset, somewhat harder than the pool, conflict cases overrepresented; prompts drafted after seeing the pool; no held-out claim.
Graders are fresh-context instances of the same model family/environment; packages delivered as isolated files (owner-approved deviation from inline delivery, audited).
Execution: request 11 (O2/arm2) HTTP 429 preserved; one owner-approved extra attempt; 15-second pacing from the resend onward (requests 1-10 used >=3-second pacing).
R1 ambiguity-aware behaviour not tested (deferred to S7-4).
Per-arm latency/token totals cover different request counts and are not comparable.
